general.labelPlaceholder: A short display label for this agent
general.readOnlyEditor: Read-only — you can only edit agents you created.
general.readOnlyViewer: Read-only — your role can view but not edit agents.
general.confirmDelete: Delete agent '{{name}}'? This removes its config and cannot be undone.
general.browserAccessHelp: Lets the agent look at and drive the browser you choose — tabs, pages, screenshots, clicks and typing — through the Wysebee Browser Probe extension. The extension asks you before acting on any site you have not marked as trusted, and has a pause switch.
general.browserAccessOffHelp: Off: the agent has no browser tools.
general.browserNotChosenHelp: Choose a browser to give the agent its browser tools. Until then it tells you how, when asked to browse.
general.browserDevtoolsOnHelp: The agent can also read the console and network log, run JavaScript in the page, change the viewport size, inspect elements, audit pages and measure performance — for building and debugging websites. Sign-in headers and cookies in network traffic are hidden. Each action follows the extension's site rules: trusted sites (such as your localhost) run it without asking, anywhere else asks you first.
general.browserDevtoolsOffHelp: Off: the agent can use pages, but not the developer tools.
general.avatarHelp: Shown in Home's menu and in the browser's side panel. An emoji, or an image you upload.
general.handleHelp: What AI apps and tasks call it. Lowercase letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter (30 at most). Renaming keeps its tools, skills, device and tasks.
general.handleInvalid: A handle starts with a lowercase letter and holds only lowercase letters, digits, - or _ (30 at most).

instructions.help: What this agent should do and how — its role, tone, rules and steps. Written in Markdown; your AI app reads them with the agent's tools, through Wysebee Assistant.
instructions.placeholder:
# Role
You are a support assistant for…

## Rules
- Always…
- Never…
instructions.tooLong: Too long: instructions can be at most {{max}} characters.

local.title: Run local program
local.short: Make a tool that runs a program on the computer paired with this agent
local.help: A template: make a tool of a program on the computer paired with this agent (a Mac or a Windows PC) — its name, what it does, the program and its arguments. Wysebee fills only the blanks you leave, and the program runs without a shell, once you allow it in Wysebee Agent on that computer.
local.intro: Wysebee can run this program when it helps. It runs exactly the program and arguments you set; Wysebee fills only the blanks, each as one argument, never through a shell.
local.name: Tool name
local.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
local.descriptionHint: Wysebee reads this to know when to use it.
local.commandHint: A full path, or the name of a program on your PATH (like git).
local.commandHintWeb: The program's full path on that computer, or the name of a program there (like git). Wysebee Agent checks it when you allow the tool.
local.noArgs: No arguments: the program runs on its own.
local.argsHint: Each argument is passed to the program as one item, in this order.
local.badName: The tool name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter (up to 40).
local.nameTaken: There is already a tool named {{name}}.
local.needDescription: Say what it does (up to 1000 characters).
local.badBlank: A blank's name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
local.emptyArg: A fixed argument needs some text, or remove it.
local.looksLikeLine: This looks like a whole command line. Program takes only the program ({{program}}); each argument goes in a row of its own below.
local.waiting: Waiting for you to allow it in Wysebee Agent on the computer
local.windowsHelp: Ready-made for Windows: a program every Windows PC has. Adding it shows you exactly what runs; it runs once you allow it in Wysebee Agent on the PC.

anyProgram.title: Run any program
anyProgram.short: Let Wysebee run any program on this Windows PC that it names
anyProgram.help: Wysebee picks the program and its arguments itself (like systeminfo, ipconfig or git), and Wysebee Agent runs it on the PC — only while you turn on "Let Wysebee run any program on this PC" there. Never through a shell, no batch files, 60 seconds at most. Use it only on a PC where you are happy for that.
anyProgram.shortMac: Let Wysebee run any program on this Mac that it names
anyProgram.helpMac: Wysebee picks the program and its arguments itself (like sw_vers, git or python3), and Wysebee Agent runs it on the Mac — only while you turn on "Let Wysebee run any program on this Mac" there. Never through a shell, 60 seconds at most, and programs that could harm the Mac are refused. Use it only on a Mac where you are happy for that.
anyProgram.shortLinux: Let Wysebee run any program on this Linux machine that it names
anyProgram.helpLinux: Wysebee picks the program and its arguments itself (like uname, df or git), and Wysebee Agent runs it on the machine — only while you turn it on there with wysebee-agent enable any-program. Never through a shell, 60 seconds at most, and programs that could harm the machine are refused. Use it only on a machine where you are happy for that.

screen.title: Screen control
screen.short: Let Wysebee see this Windows PC's screen and use its mouse and keyboard
screen.help: Wysebee takes screenshots of the PC's screen and clicks, types and scrolls there, as you would — for trying an app on the PC. A red ring shows where it clicks. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee see and control this PC's screen" in Wysebee Agent there.
screen.shortMac: Let Wysebee see this Mac's screen and use its mouse and keyboard
screen.helpMac: Wysebee takes screenshots of the Mac's screen and clicks, types and scrolls there, as you would — for trying an app on the Mac, or in the iOS Simulator. A red ring shows where it clicks. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee see and control this Mac's screen" in Wysebee Agent there, and allow it Screen Recording and Accessibility in macOS.

developer.title: Developer access
developer.short: Let Wysebee work on this Windows PC as a coding assistant would
developer.help: Wysebee runs PowerShell and cmd commands (builds and tests in the background too) and reads, edits and searches files anywhere on the PC, as you. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee use this PC as a developer" in Wysebee Agent there.
developer.shortMac: Let Wysebee work on this Mac as a coding assistant would
developer.helpMac: Wysebee runs zsh, bash and sh commands (builds and tests in the background too) and reads, edits and searches files anywhere on the Mac, as you. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee use this Mac as a developer" in Wysebee Agent there.
developer.shortLinux: Let Wysebee work on this Linux machine as a coding assistant would
developer.helpLinux: Wysebee runs bash, zsh and sh commands (builds and tests in the background too) and reads, edits and searches files anywhere on the machine, as you. It works only while you turn it on there with wysebee-agent enable developer.

androidToolkit.title: Android Development Toolkit
androidToolkit.short: Let Wysebee use the Android phones plugged in to this Windows PC, through adb
androidToolkit.help: Screenshots, what is on screen, logcat, apps and files; tapping, swiping and typing; installing and uninstalling apps, pushing files and adb shell — on the phones and emulators adb sees on the PC. Never root or the bootloader. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee use Android phones on this PC" in Wysebee Agent there.
androidToolkit.shortMac: Let Wysebee use the Android phones plugged in to this Mac, through adb
androidToolkit.helpMac: Screenshots, what is on screen, logcat, apps and files; tapping, swiping and typing; installing and uninstalling apps, pushing files and adb shell — on the phones and emulators adb sees on the Mac (adb comes with Android Studio, or brew install android-platform-tools). Never root or the bootloader. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee use Android phones on this Mac" in Wysebee Agent there.
androidToolkit.shortLinux: Let Wysebee use the Android phones plugged in to this Linux machine, through adb
androidToolkit.helpLinux: Screenshots, what is on screen, logcat, apps and files; tapping, swiping and typing; installing and uninstalling apps, pushing files and adb shell — on the phones and emulators adb sees on the machine (sudo apt install adb, or Android Studio's). Never root or the bootloader. It works only while you turn it on there with wysebee-agent enable android.

iosToolkit.title: iPhone Development Toolkit
iosToolkit.short: Let Wysebee use this Mac's iOS simulators and paired iPhones, through Xcode
iosToolkit.help: Lists simulators and iPhones; a simulator's screenshots and log; the apps on each; boots and shuts down simulators, opens links, launches and stops apps, switches light and dark mode; installs and uninstalls apps. Taps in a simulator go through Screen control. Needs Xcode. It works only while you turn on "Let Wysebee use iPhones and simulators on this Mac" in Wysebee Agent there.

gmail.title: Open Gmail
gmail.short: Let Wysebee open and read your Gmail in your browser
gmail.help: Add your Gmail inboxes — a link to each and what it is for. When you ask about that mail, Wysebee opens the right one in your browser, where you are signed in to Gmail, and reads it.
gmail.intro: Add a link for each Gmail you use and say what it is for: Wysebee reads these to choose which to open. It opens it in your browser and reads what it shows; the browser extension still asks before it acts on a site you have not trusted.
gmail.linkHint: Open the inbox in your browser and copy its address — it starts with https://mail.google.com/.
gmail.descriptionPlaceholder: My work mail, from clients and the team

sites.browserIntro: This is read in your browser, where you are signed in. Connect Wysebee to your browser first — or set it up later.
sites.waiting: Waiting for the extension… This continues by itself as soon as it connects.
sites.noBrowser: Wysebee has no browser yet: it can open these links once one is set up under Browser access.
sites.badLink: {{item}}: give a link that starts with https://.
sites.badGmailLink: {{item}}: give a link that starts with https://mail.google.com/.
sites.twice: {{item}}: that link is already in the list.
sites.suggesting: Reading your bookmarks… Your browser may ask you first.
sites.suggestNone: Nothing in your bookmarks looks like this.
sites.suggestNeedsBrowser: Choose a browser to see suggestions from its bookmarks.

calendar.title: Open Calendar
calendar.short: Let Wysebee open and read your calendars in your browser
calendar.help: Add your calendars — a link to each and what it is for. When you ask what is coming up, Wysebee opens the right one in your browser, where you are signed in, and reads it.
calendar.intro: Add a link for each calendar you use (Google Calendar, Outlook…) and say what it is for: Wysebee reads these to choose which to open, then reads it in your browser.
calendar.linkHint: Open the calendar in your browser and copy its address.
calendar.descriptionPlaceholder: My work calendar: meetings and deadlines

travel.title: Travel
travel.short: Let Wysebee look up trips on your travel sites
travel.help: Add the travel sites you use — airlines, hotels, booking sites — and what each is for. When you ask about a trip, Wysebee opens the right one in your browser and searches it there; it never books or pays without you.
travel.intro: Add a link for each travel site you use and say what it is for: Wysebee reads these to choose which to open, then searches it in your browser.
travel.linkHint: A site's address, like https://www.booking.com/ or your airline's.

news.title: News
news.short: Let Wysebee read the news sites you follow
news.help: Add the news sites you read and what each is for. When you ask for the news, Wysebee opens the right one in your browser and sums it up.
news.intro: Add a link for each news site you read and say what it is for: Wysebee reads these to choose which to open, then reads it in your browser.

website.title: Website
website.short: Let Wysebee open and read websites you name
website.help: Add any websites you want Wysebee to use — a link to each and what it is for. When you ask about one, Wysebee opens it in your browser and reads it.
website.intro: Add a link for each website and say what it is for: Wysebee reads these to choose which to open, then reads it in your browser.
website.linkHint: The page's address, starting with https://.
website.descriptionPlaceholder: Our team's wiki: how we do things

folder.title: Local Folder
folder.short: Let Wysebee find and read files in a folder on this computer
folder.help: A template: add a folder on this computer and whether Wysebee may only read it or also write text files there. Wysebee can then find files by name and read text, Word, Excel and PDF files; a picture is shown to you in the chat, not to the AI. Files are never uploaded.
folder.intro: Wysebee can find files in this folder (and the folders in it) and read them: text, Word, Excel and PDF. A picture is shown to you in the chat only.
folder.writeHelp: Also write text files here (and make folders), when you ask.
folder.descriptionPlaceholder: My work documents: reports, budgets and contracts
folder.private: Files never leave this computer as files. What Wysebee reads is passed to the AI for that answer, and is not kept in your conversations in Wysebee Cloud.
folder.badPath: Give the folder's full path, or choose it with Browse….
folder.tooLong: Say what it holds in at most 1000 characters.
folder.onMac: Add, change or remove folders in Wysebee Agent on the computer.

tools.noneYet: No tools yet. Add one from the Tool library.

postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.short: Let the agent query a PostgreSQL database
postgres.help: A template: add a PostgreSQL database by its server, database and user. The agent can then read its tables and run queries — read only, unless you allow changes. The password is kept encrypted: on the computer, or in Wysebee Cloud for an agent living there.
postgres.intro: Connected to an agent, this database is queried by the SQL Query tools you write on it — the AI never sees the connection itself. Use a database user with only the rights you want it to have.
postgres.name: Name
postgres.passwordSaved: Saved — leave empty to keep it
postgres.changesHelp: Without it, every statement runs in a read-only transaction. With it, the agent may insert, update and delete — as far as the user's rights allow.
postgres.descriptionPlaceholder: Orders and customers of the web shop
postgres.badName: The name is a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or _, at most 30.
postgres.taken: Another connection already has that name.
postgres.badHost: Give the server's host, like db.example.com (no spaces).
postgres.badPort: The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
postgres.tooLong: Say what it holds in at most 1000 characters.

sslHelp.verify: Encrypted, and the server's certificate is checked against the public certificate authorities.
sslHelp.require: Encrypted, but anyone answering at that address is accepted: for a server with its own certificate authority.

postgres.publicOnly: Wysebee Cloud connects to it, always encrypted, and reaches only databases with a public address.
postgres.cloudPrivate: The password is kept in Wysebee Cloud, encrypted, and never shown again. What the agent reads is passed to the AI for that answer.
postgres.confirmRemove: Remove the connection {{name}}? Its saved password is deleted too.

snowflake.title: Snowflake
snowflake.short: Let the agent query your Snowflake data
snowflake.help: A template: add a Snowflake database by its account and database. The agent can then read its tables and run queries — read only, unless you allow changes. Its access token or key is kept encrypted: on your computers, or in Wysebee Cloud for an agent living there.
snowflake.intro: Connected to an agent, this database is queried by the SQL Query tools you write on it — the AI never sees the connection itself. Use a role with only the rights you want it to have. Snowflake bills you for the warehouse time its queries use.
snowflake.accountHelp: Your account identifier, as in your Snowflake address: myorg-myaccount.snowflakecomputing.com.
snowflake.secretSaved: Saved — leave empty to keep it

secretHelp.token: Made in Snowflake under your user's settings, Programmatic access tokens. Snowflake no longer takes a password here.
secretHelp.key: The unencrypted private key whose public key is registered on the Snowflake user. Wysebee signs a short-lived token with it for each call.

snowflake.changesHelp: Without it, only statements that read are sent (SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN). With it, the agent may insert, update and delete — as far as the role's rights allow.
snowflake.badAccount: Give the account identifier, like myorg-myaccount (letters, digits, - _ . only).
snowflake.badWord: The warehouse, schema and role have no spaces.
snowflake.badUser: Give the user name the key belongs to (no spaces).
snowflake.confirmRemove: Remove the connection {{name}}? Its saved token or key is deleted too.
snowflake.cloudPrivate: The token or key is kept in Wysebee Cloud, encrypted, and never shown again. What the agent reads is passed to the AI for that answer.

macPaired.unknown: Runs on the computer paired with this agent

sql.title: SQL Query
sql.short: A query you write, with inputs the agent fills in
sql.help: A template: write a SQL query with input parameters, run on one of the agent's database connections. The agent calls it by its name and gives the parameters; their values are always passed separately, never written into the SQL.
sql.noConnection: A SQL Query tool runs on one of this agent's database connections, and it has none yet. Add a PostgreSQL or Snowflake connection on the agent's General tab, then come back to write the tool.
sql.idHelp: This tool's permanent identifier — never changes, even when you rename it below.
sql.name: Name
sql.nameHelp: Identifies this tool to the AI — may contain letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, and must start and end with a letter, digit or underscore. Safe to rename anytime.
sql.descriptionPlaceholder: What the tool computes — shown to the agent to help it pick the tool.
sql.connectionGone: Not connected to this agent any more — pick another
sql.connectionHelp: One of this agent's connections, set on its General tab.
sql.paramDescriptionPlaceholder: Description for the AI assistant: what this input is and where its values come from
sql.paramDescriptionHelp: The AI reads this to know what to pass: say what the value means, its format, and where it can find it.
sql.optionalHelp: When the AI leaves it out, the filter is dropped. Put the condition inside [[ ]] in the SQL, e.g. [[AND COLUMN = {{example}}]].
sql.templateHelp: Write {param} for a parameter and {database} for the connection's database. Wrap a filter whose parameter is only set sometimes in [[ ]]. One statement; read only unless the connection allows changes.
sql.valid: Valid — the database accepts this query (it was not run).
sql.notConnected: Its database is not connected to this agent
sql.badName: The name has letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starts and ends with a letter, digit or underscore, and is at most 64 characters.
sql.taken: Another SQL tool already has that name.
sql.needDescription: Say what the tool computes: the AI picks the tool by it.
sql.needConnection: Pick the database connection it queries.
sql.badParam: Each parameter's name is a letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (and not 'database').
sql.twoParams: Two parameters have the same name.
sql.draftBadge: Draft from your AI app — review it
sql.draftNote: Your AI app drafted this tool. Read the SQL and its parameters, Validate it, and click Create tool to let the agent use it. Until then the agent does not have it.
sql.confirmDiscard: Discard the draft '{{name}}'? It is deleted.
sql.changeNote: Your AI app proposed a new version of this tool, shown below. The agent goes on using the tool as it is until you click Apply change.

proposals.title: Proposed by your AI app
proposals.note: Nothing here is used until you accept it. Check each one: a tool, a change or a switch decides what this agent can do.
proposals.programNote: Once created, Wysebee Agent on the computer asks you again before it runs.
proposals.changeNote: The agent uses the tool as it is until you apply the change.
proposals.switchWarn: What it allows: {{help}} Turning it on takes effect when you click Save.
proposals.skillFiles: See its files on the Skills page first
proposals.instructionNote: Every AI app reads this agent's Instruction before using it. Review puts this one on the Instruction tab for you to edit, then Save.

aiApp.title: Connect your AI app
aiApp.description: Use this agent from your own AI app, Claude or ChatGPT, through Wysebee Assistant. Add its address once: your AI app then reaches every agent you leave on, and the page you open with Wysebee Assistant in Workspaces. Run by Wysebee Cloud: no Wysebee Desktop needed.
aiApp.howTo: In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Create. Then sign in with this same Wysebee account when it asks.
aiApp.privacy: Only an AI app signed in to your Wysebee account is let in. Tool calls and their results pass through Wysebee Cloud and aren't kept. Your browser's Wysebee Agent extension and Wysebee Agent on your computer still decide what runs, and may ask you first.
aiApp.urlLabel: Add this address as a custom connector (MCP server) in your AI app:
aiApp.offers: Your AI app gets this agent's {{tools}} tools and {{skills}} skills.
aiApp.expose: Let your AI app use this agent
aiApp.exposed: Your AI app can use it
aiApp.hidden: Turned off for your AI app
aiApp.offNote: Turned off: your AI app neither sees nor uses this agent.

skills.tabIntro: Tick the skills this agent has: it loads one when a request calls for it. A tick is saved at once. Skills are kept in your account in Wysebee Cloud, with their files, and reach a paired computer too.
skills.empty: No skills yet. Make one with New skill.

connections.title: Database connections
connections.help: Databases this agent can reach. The AI never sees a connection itself: it queries one only through the SQL Query tools you write on it (Tools → Database).
connections.confirmRemove: Disconnect '{{name}}' from this agent? Its SQL Query tools on it stop working here. The connection stays in your account.
connections.confirmDelete: Delete the connection '{{name}}'? It is removed from every agent that has it, with its saved password, token or key. This cannot be undone.
connections.inUse_one: This connection can't be deleted while a SQL Query tool uses it. Delete that tool, or move it to another connection, first:
connections.inUse_other: This connection can't be deleted while SQL Query tools use it. Delete those tools, or move them to another connection, first:
